differences.title: 1. GRANULARITY
differences.leftDesc: React tracks state updates per component render function. When state changes, React schedules a rerender of the component subtree, then reconciles changes by diffing the resulting virtual DOM output.
differences.rightDesc: SolidJS compiles JSX into fine-grained computations. Signals form a dependency graph; only computations that read a changed signal rerun, avoiding whole-tree rerenders and minimizing reconciliation overhead.

differences.title: 2. CHANGE DETECTION
differences.leftDesc: Updates originate from calls like useState setters or dispatching actions. React then re-executes the component to derive new props/state values and decides what DOM updates are needed through reconciliation.
differences.rightDesc: Reads of signals inside computations automatically register dependencies. When a signal changes, SolidJS notifies only downstream computations, updating derived values and the DOM bindings directly.

differences.title: 3. DERIVED STATE
differences.leftDesc: React uses useMemo/useCallback as performance hints, and correctness still depends on dependency arrays. Derived values recompute when dependencies change, but memoization can be bypassed by misuse or unstable references.
differences.rightDesc: SolidJS provides memoized derived signals via createMemo. Computations rerun only when their specific dependencies change, and the runtime tracks them precisely without relying on developer-provided dependency arrays.

differences.title: 4. RENDER OUTPUT MODEL
differences.leftDesc: React renders by producing a new React element tree each time a component renders. Reconciliation compares previous and next trees to determine which DOM mutations to apply.
differences.rightDesc: SolidJS compiles templates into DOM nodes once. Reactive computations update node properties/text directly when dependencies change, so there’s no virtual element tree diffing on each update.

differences.title: 5. BATCHING & FLUSHING
differences.leftDesc: React batches state updates and uses a scheduler to coordinate rendering work. Depending on mode and updates, React may defer, interrupt, or coalesce renders before committing changes to the DOM.
differences.rightDesc: SolidJS signal updates trigger propagation through the dependency graph in a predictable order. Computations rerun and commit DOM updates without the same render-scheduler model, typically yielding immediate, deterministic results.

differences.title: 6. STALE DATA PITFALLS
differences.leftDesc: Hook closures can capture outdated values if effects or callbacks depend on the wrong dependencies. Bugs often appear as stale state in event handlers, effects, or async flows.
differences.rightDesc: Because computations read signals at runtime (not during a one-time render), reactive values stay current. Event handlers can reference signals directly, reducing stale-closure risk while still requiring care with async boundaries.

differences.title: 7. PERFORMANCE SHAPE
differences.leftDesc: With hooks, changing any state typically rerenders the component and its descendants (subject to memoization). Large component trees can accumulate render and reconciliation work, even if only a small leaf changes.
differences.rightDesc: Signal-based fine-grained reactivity keeps updates localized to the exact computations that depend on changed data. This shifts performance from subtree rerender costs toward minimal dependency-driven recomputation.
